artworks.title: Mercury, Herse, and Aglaurus
artworks.description: Lagrenée's Nationalmuseum canvas: Mercury at the threshold, Herse the prize, Aglauros the envious sister who will turn to stone — Ovid's Cecropid triangle.

artworks.title: Mercury, Herse, and Aglauros
artworks.description: Poussin's ENSBA drawing compresses Metamorphoses II into a doorway drama — Mercury, Herse, and the sister who bars the god.

artworks.title: Hermes and Herse
artworks.description: Attic red-figure cup (Louvre G494): Hermes pursues Herse — the desire that makes Aglauros' envy fatal in Ovid's later telling.

artworks.title: Lekythos with Hermes and Herse
artworks.description: White-ground lekythos (Madrid): Hermes and Herse meet — the named encounter before Roman poets thicken the jealousy plot with Aglauros' stone.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book II stages Mercury's bribe, Minerva's Envy, and Aglauros turned to stone — the jealous sister who bars the god from her sibling Herse.

popCulture.title: Aglaurus, daughter of Cecrops
popCulture.description: Cecrops' middle daughter remains Ovid's emblem of envy punished — the Athenian princess who opens Pandora's box of spite and ends as rock.

popCulture.title: Herse
popCulture.description: The fairest Cecropid Mercury sought — Herse's beauty and Aglauros' gatekeeping keep the Athenian sisters paired in reception.
